title: Shadowmoon Valley
body: Shadowmoon Valley lies in the far southeast of Outland, a land of ash, black rock and rivers of green fel lava under a dim and smoky sky. The orcs of the Shadowmoon clan once honored their ancestors here, and at its eastern edge the draenei raised the Temple of Karabor, one of their holiest sites. Both were lost to the Horde. Gul'dan's warriors took Karabor and the Shadow Council made it their seat, and the warlock raised the volcano at the valley's center in a ritual that severed the orcs from the elements of Draenor. The temple, now called the Black Temple, is the throne of Illidan Stormrage, and his servants, fel orcs and naga, Broken and blood elves, hold the valley in his name. The Burning Legion bombards it from Legion Hold. Against them stand the Wildhammer dwarves, the Horde's Kor'kron, and the Aldor and Scryers of Shattrath, while the Netherwing drakes struggle against the Dragonmaw orcs who enslave them.

title: Wildhammer Stronghold
body: Wildhammer Stronghold stands in the southwest of the valley, the fortress of Kurdran Wildhammer, thane of the Wildhammer in Outland, and his gryphon riders. It is a hard place to hold. Infernals fall on its walls from Legion Hold to the northwest, Illidan's minions press from the other side, and Wing Commander Nuainn's riders have fought so long without relief that they are ragged with exhaustion. The ground itself is restless: the stronghold was built over the ancestral grounds of the Shadowmoon orcs, and the spirits of the old clan, dormant for nearly twenty years, now wander its courtyards. Zorus the Judicator studies them, while the gnome Gnomus, an inventor turned gourmand, dreams only of food that never cools.

title: Shadowmoon Village
body: Shadowmoon Village is the Horde's outpost in the northwest of the valley, held by Overlord Or'barokh and the elite Kor'kron guard. Like the dwarves to the south it lives under the Legion's guns: infernals from Legion Hold to the southwest rain on its walls, and Blood Guard Gulmok drafts every able fighter onto the line. The village is haunted as well. Chief Apothecary Hildagard has crafted goggles that reveal the ghosts of Shadowmoon zealots drifting among the buildings, and what she learns from them leaves her badly shaken. Nearby, the blood elf Researcher Tiorus studies the heat-proof diemetradons of the lava flows with probes built by his former partner, the gnome Gnomus, who resents it.

title: Legion Hold
body: Legion Hold is the Burning Legion's fortress in western Shadowmoon, the source of the infernals that pound both the Wildhammer and the Horde outposts. Warbringer Razuun directs its war in the name of Doom Lord Kazzak, and his order to the hold's commander was plain: destroy the orcish and dwarven strongholds with all haste. Terrormasters and Shadow Council warlocks guard the stockpiled infernals, and the pit lords Makazradon and Morgroron bear glaives forged to slay demons. Beside the hold, the Fetid Pool festers around the wreckage of a fallen fel reaver. A teleporter in the hold leads to Invasion Point: Cataclysm, high in the northern mountains, where the Legion masses still more infernals under the guard of fel reaver sentinels.

title: The Deathforge
body: The Deathforge is a Shadow Council foundry dug into the rock between the two outposts, where infernals are made as fast as the Legion can hurl them. Mo'arg smiths work the forges, and in a summoning chamber below ground the warlocks call up the corrupted elementals that become the burning hearts of the infernals. Two scouting parties watch from the heights, the dwarves of Deathforge Tower and the orcs of Slag Watch, under strict orders to observe and not to fight. Each lost one of its own inside: the Wildhammer Flanis Swiftwing, who volunteered to spy, and the orc Kagrosh, who wanted to be a hero. Neither came back, and their bodies lie where the forge's keepers left them.

title: Illidari Point
body: Illidari Point lies in the southwest, between Legion Hold and Wildhammer Stronghold. It is the proving ground for Illidan's demons, those who abandoned the Burning Legion to serve the Betrayer, and satyrs, shadowstalkers and succubi gather there under his lieutenant Lothros. Succubi led by Painmistress Gabrissa work their rituals around a rune ringed by hovering crystals, and hidden in the ether at the back of the point lurks a creature called Veneratus the Many. Here Ar'tor, the youngest son of Oronok Torn-heart, came hunting a piece of the Cipher of Damnation. He was found dead, his body held in the air above the rune by beams from the demonic crystals.

title: Sketh'lon and the Magma Fields
body: The Sketh'lon arakkoa once camped in western Shadowmoon. When the Horde massed under Gul'dan they planned to strike at him first, and the warlock answered with a spell that destroyed their camps and twisted their spirits. Their ruins remain: the Sketh'lon Wreckage northwest of the Deathforge, and the Sketh'lon Base Camp to the south, east of Wildhammer Stronghold. Their ghosts linger as the Dark Conclave, and they prey on the orc peons sent to cut wood among the ruins, draining their lives to feed their magic. Between the two outposts the road crosses the Magma Fields, where lava flows through cracks in the ground and felfire diemetradons bask in the heat.

title: The Hand of Gul'dan
body: The Hand of Gul'dan is the great volcano at the center of the valley, raised by the warlock Gul'dan in the ritual that tore the orcs away from the elements. Fel lava still pours down its sides, and its lava long ago buried the draenei village of Baa'ri. On its flanks the Fel Pits seethe with enraged spirits of fire and earth, and the Ashtongue Corruptors Eykenen and Uylaru, once shaman who now defile the elements they revered, tend corrupt totems among them. The Scalding Pools lie near the summit. Spectral riders, the Ghostriders of Karabor, circle the mountain on the roads around its base, and the fel beast Uvuros, wanted dead by both outposts, prowls its slopes.

title: The Altar of Damnation
body: On the western outskirts of the Hand of Gul'dan stands the Altar of Damnation, where Gul'dan spoke the words that shattered this land. The moment has left its mark. A memory of the warlock still stands at the altar among the kneeling spirits of the damned, and beside him linger remnants of his hate, greed, malice, pride and corruption. Earthmender Torlok and Earthmender Gorboto of the Earthen Ring keep watch there, seeking to commune with the tortured elements. Gul'dan was not content to destroy the draenei, Torlok says: he razed Draenor itself and siphoned off its energies for his war, and all that is left here are the remnants of his madness.

title: Coilskar Point
body: Coilskar Point and the cistern to its east are the lair of the Coilskar naga, servants of Illidan, who have seized the only clean water left in Shadowmoon Valley. They foul it for their own ends, and the agitated pools around their villages howl with the anguish of enraged water spirits. The earthmender Wilda came seeking the source of the spirits' distress and was taken prisoner, held in a watery cell beside other captive spirits. Lady Shav'rar commands at the point, and Coilskar sorceresses guard the cistern. It was here, too, that the naga hid one fragment of the Cipher of Damnation in their chests, a secret Grom'tor, eldest son of Oronok, beat out of a Coilskar commander.

title: Oronok's Farm
body: High on the Shattered Shelf above Coilskar Cistern, a weathered orc keeps a campfire and a herd of trained felboars. He calls himself Oronok Torn-heart, hermit and farmer, and his boars root tubers out of the hard earth of the Shattered Plains below. The plains are not kind to farmers: ravenous flayers from a nest to the northeast prey on his animals, and a flayer matriarch guards their eggs. Oronok invites travelers to warm themselves by his fire and warns them of the beasts of the shelf. Few guess that the farmer's life is a disguise, or that this quiet old orc once stood at Gul'dan's side.

title: Ruins of Baa'ri
body: Baa'ri was a draenei village, rich in relics of religious importance, until the Hand of Gul'dan rose and buried it under lava with its people. Now Illidan has set the Ashtongue Broken to dig it out. Scores of Ashtongue workers labor in the ruins under Illidari overseers and Akama's lieutenant, Oronu the Elder, and handlers drive elekk demolishers through the rubble. Among the treasures they seek are the Tablets of Baa'ri, said to hold the secrets of the Temple of Karabor, and the fragments of a Medallion of Karabor, which once let the highest draenei priests pass freely into the temple. The Aldor and the Scryers both send agents to reach them first.

title: The Warden's Cage
body: South of the Ruins of Baa'ri, the Warden's Cage is a prison run by Akama and his Ashtongue Deathsworn, whispered among his enemies to be a torture chamber. Its most important captive is Maiev Shadowsong, the Warden who pursued Illidan to Outland, now held in a cell she swears will not keep her. A satyr named Zandras watches the prison from above its walls on Illidan's behalf, and the demon Vagath has orders from Illidan to keep a close eye on the Warden. What the watchers do not see lies beyond the halls, through a passage hidden by stagnant water: a secret chamber where Akama takes counsel with the few he trusts.

title: Altar of Sha'tar
body: The Altar of Sha'tar is the Aldor's outpost in Shadowmoon, standing northwest of the Black Temple. From here the draenei priesthood carries its war against Illidan and the Legion to their very doorstep. Exarch Onaala, who trained as an anchorite in days when female exarchs were all but unheard of, leads the outpost, holding that courage and conviction count for more than anything else. Anchorite Ceyla studies the secrets of Karabor, Vindicator Aluumen sends fighters against the Ashtongue at Baa'ri and the fel orcs on the holy Ata'mal Terrace, and Harbinger Saronen gathers the insignias of the Legion's officers. The Dragonmaw would gladly see the altar burned, for it blocks their way to Coilskar.

title: Ruins of Karabor
body: The Ruins of Karabor lie before the walls of the Black Temple, and Illidan has turned them into a training ground for demon hunters. Sunfury blood elves, soldiers of Prince Kael'thas, arrive in numbers to learn his art, dressing and fighting like Illidan himself, while Sunfury warlocks summon and bind demons for the initiates to battle. Their master is Varedis, the one blood elf of Kael's first five to survive Illidan's trials, and with him serve the three night elf demon hunters who trained him, Alandien, Theras and Netharel. One prisoner is too dangerous even for these lessons: the pit lord Azaloth, held banished in the ruins and seething at his captors.

title: Ata'mal Terrace
body: The Ata'mal Terrace beside the Black Temple was once one of the draenei's holiest sites, where ata'mal crystals were used in their spiritual ceremonies. Now the fel orcs of the Shadowmoon clan, Illidan's most feared army, hold it. Slayers, chosen and darkweavers crowd its tiers alongside shadowsworn drakonid, and they have dug special ore from the sacred ground to forge corrupted arms. The orcs keep a secret: an ata'mal crystal called the Heart of Fury, clouded in dark magic to hide it from the Sha'tar. Shadowlord Deathwail circles above the terrace, out of reach, and swears its power belongs to Illidan.

title: The Black Temple
body: The Black Temple was once the Temple of Karabor, the great sanctuary of the draenei. Gul'dan's Horde took it, the Shadow Council made it their seat, and the warlock kept his private quarters inside. Later the pit lord Magtheridon ruled from it, until Illidan Stormrage drove him out with the help of Akama's Broken and claimed the temple as his throne. The ghosts of the clerics of Karabor, murdered by Teron Gorefiend after the city fell, still roam before its walls. Now the naaru Xi'ri gathers Aldor and Scryer soldiers on the approach to the temple, and before its walls stalks Doomwalker, the fel reaver Kil'jaeden sent against its gates.

title: Netherwing Fields
body: East of the Hand of Gul'dan, fields of enormous blue crystals jut from the earth, and nether drakes wheel above them. These are the Netherwing, a young flight born of black dragon eggs that were steeped in raw nether energy. They are frightened now, too afraid of the Dragonmaw to come down even to feed, and some fall dead from exhaustion; Mordenai, himself one of the flight, does what he can to save them. Rocknail flayers, the drakes' natural prey, swarm among the crystals. Past the fields, Netherwing Pass leads on to the Altar of Shadows, a lonely shrine where an ancient Shadowmoon spirit was long kept prisoner under the eye of Karsius the Ancient Watcher.

title: Sanctum of the Stars
body: The Sanctum of the Stars is the Scryers' outpost in Shadowmoon, standing at the foot of the Netherwing Fields. For these blood elves the war runs on two fronts: against Illidan, and against the Sunfury of Prince Kael'thas, whose ranks keep swelling with pilgrims from Quel'Thalas. Battlemage Vyara warns that the Scryers must outrecruit Kael or, once recruits run short, outkill him. Arcanist Thelis and Larissa Sunstrike pursue Illidan's secrets, and Varen the Reclaimer leads strikes on the Ashtongue and on the Ata'mal fel orcs, who once fell on the sanctum in a savage attack. The Dragonmaw covet the site, since it cuts their lines to Eclipse Point and Illidari Point.

title: Eclipse Point
body: Eclipse Point is a terraced ruin in the south of the valley, held by the Eclipsion, blood elves in Illidan's service under Grand Commander Ruusk. Its dragonhawks see through disguises. The elves guard their charges closely: the Rod of Lianthe lies locked in a strongbox in a pavilion on the top tier, and they kept watch over a third of the Cipher of Damnation, moving it from place to place on Illidan's written orders. Each day an envoy comes from the Black Temple with those orders, and from the shadows of the bridge to the north, Borak, son of Oronok, has watched the elves for weeks, waiting for a moment when the envoy's bodyguard is gone.

title: The Path of Conquest
body: The Path of Conquest lies just east of Eclipse Point, and there Illidan's Eclipsion armies muster soldiers, cavaliers and spellbinders for a great advance. At its southern end, by a stationary caravan, Chancellor Bloodleaf sought to win Corok the Mighty and the giants of Shadowmoon to Illidan's side, reminding them that Illidan's enemies are destroyed. The crazed colossi of the Eclipsion Fields to the west are the children of Behemothon, King of the Colossi, who will not forgive an attack on them. Also at the path's southern end stands Crimson Watch, held by the Crimson Sigil, Illidan's elite, where Marcus Auralion, High General of the Sha'tar, was shut inside a crystal prison after Val'zareq the Conqueror captured him.

title: Dragonmaw Fortress
body: Dragonmaw Fortress rises on the eastern edge of the Netherwing Fields, the stronghold of the Dragonmaw orcs who serve Illidan. Here the clan does to the nether drakes what it once did to the red dragons of Azeroth: wranglers and subjugators capture them and torture them until they bend, and many broken drakes now carry Dragonmaw drake-riders into battle. Atop the fortress, bound in chains that sap her strength, Karynaku, mate of Neltharaku and mother of the flight, is held prisoner. Her jailer is the clan's chieftain, the ancient orc Zuluhed the Whacked, who hides in her thoughts and waits for her to break.
sources: quest 10836 description (fortress on the eastern edge of the Netherwing Fields; some drakes corrupted by the Dragonmaw)

title: Netherwing Ledge
body: Netherwing Ledge was once part of the Shadowmoon mainland; now it floats in the sky off the valley's broken southeastern shelf. It was the Netherwing's sanctuary until the Dragonmaw took it. At Dragonmaw Base Camp, Overlord Mor'ghor drives peons and Murkblood Broken to strip the island of its crystals, ore and netherdust pollen to supply Illidan's armies, and transporters carry the haul to the fortress along the Dragonmaw Skyway. Above the ledge the drake Vhel'kur, spawn of Deathwing, flies an endless circle around the island that was his home and is now his grave, still seething at his defeat by Teron Gorefiend.
sources: quest 10634 description (once part of the mainland, now a floating island; Vhel'kur, spawn of Deathwing, defeated by Gorefiend)

title: Netherwing Mines
body: The Netherwing Mines bore deep into Netherwing Ledge, where the Dragonmaw set Murkblood Broken to dig. The work stopped when a miner's pick struck a crystal formation that turned out to be part of a sleeping nether dragon, Toranaku. The dragon woke in fury and slaughtered the workers, the creatures of the depths rose with it, and a band of miners cut off from the exit soon sank into madness. The Dragonmaw call it a grim discovery. The Murkblood know better. Offered peace and protection by the Netherwing, they helped Toranaku rouse the creatures of the mine, at great cost, hoping to make the mine unlivable and drive the orcs from the island.

title: Kurdran Wildhammer
body: Kurdran Wildhammer is the thane of the Wildhammer dwarves in Outland. In the Second War he fought the Horde on the back of his gryphon, Sky'ree, and was credited with slaying nine dragons. When the Alliance expedition crossed the Dark Portal he led its gryphon riders, and when Ner'zhul's portals began to tear Draenor apart he chose to stay behind with his comrades so that the Portal could be sealed. Azeroth mourned him as dead for twenty years. He and Sky'ree survived, and now he holds Wildhammer Stronghold against the Legion's siege, receiving visitors inside while his keeper tends the faithful gryphon who would die for him.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Kurdran_Wildhammer (Second War, Sky'ree, nine dragons, Gryphon Rider Division, stayed to ensure the Portal was sealed, presumed dead twenty years, Thane of Wildhammer Stronghold)

title: Overlord Or'barokh
body: Overlord Or'barokh commands Shadowmoon Village for the Horde, with the elite Kor'kron guard at his back. Caught between the Legion's infernals and Illidan's armies, he has no men to spare and says so bluntly: when a shaman came pleading for soldiers, he asked whether the shaman had no eyes for the demons at the door and advised a prayer to the gods instead, for the Horde could not help. What he does have are recruits, and every newcomer is a grunt to him. His wind riders brought word of the Eclipsion armies mustering on the Path of Conquest, and it was his plan, with a potion brewed by Researcher Tiorus, that turned the giants of Shadowmoon against Illidan's elves.
sources: quest 10595 description (elite Kor'kron guard)

title: Earthmender Torlok
body: Earthmender Torlok of the Earthen Ring keeps vigil at the Altar of Damnation, trying to make amends to the elements of Shadowmoon. He is an orc, and he does not hide that it was his own people who wounded them: here, he says, Gul'dan severed the tie between the orcs and the spirits, and not content with the ruin of the draenei, razed Draenor itself for power. The spirits he finds are enraged and unwilling to speak, so he gathers their souls in a totem until they can be heard. When at last they answer, they name a firelord unearthed by Gul'dan's ritual, and Torlok, with no idea where to turn, sends for an old hermit he once met.
sources: npc_text 10250 (Gul'dan severed the tie; razed Draenor)

title: Oronok Torn-heart
body: Oronok Torn-heart lives as a hermit farmer above Coilskar Cistern, and admits that he has been a lot of things. One of them was a lieutenant of Gul'dan. A shaman who had abandoned the elements for shadow magic, he stood beside the warlock at the Altar of Damnation when the land was shattered, and like every orc on Draenor he felt the cut, a loss too deep for words. Sick at heart, he gathered his boys and fled to the hills. It has taken him twenty years to reach the elements again. When he learned what Illidan had done with Gul'dan's words, he sent his three sons, Grom'tor the warrior, Ar'tor the hunter and Borak the scholar, to recover them.
sources: quest 10514 description (I've been a lot of things)

title: Akama
body: Akama leads the Ashtongue, the most feared tribe of the Broken, and to many of his own people he is a traitor and Illidan's lapdog. He lets them think so. He joined Illidan, he says, because visions foretold that his race would otherwise be destroyed, and he has waited ever since for further signs: Velen's exodus, the opening of the Dark Portal, the coming of heroes from Azeroth. The brutes he sends to Baa'ri were chosen to keep up the mask he shows Illidan, but his Deathsworn know his true mind. Illidan holds Akama's very soul prisoner within the Black Temple, so the Broken leader plots in secret in the Warden's Cage, guarding Maiev Shadowsong and biding his time.
sources: npc_text 10447 (known as a traitor, Illidan's lapdog)
quest 10619 description (Ashtongue feared among all Broken)

title: Maiev Shadowsong
body: Maiev Shadowsong is the Warden who held Illidan captive for ten thousand years and hunted him all the way to Outland after he escaped. Now she is the prisoner, locked in a cell in the Warden's Cage under the watch of Akama and his Deathsworn. Akama insists that they want the same thing and that she must wait, for he has spent years preparing and cannot tip his hand too soon. Maiev will have none of it. She is no pawn in his game, she tells him, and when she unleashes her wrath on Illidan it will have nothing to do with his foolish scheme. If Illidan is to die, it will be by her hand.
sources: creature_text 21699 (release me; if Illidan is to die it shall be by my hand; not a pawn in your game; cell won't hold me)

title: Neltharaku
body: Neltharaku is the patron of the Netherwing, a nether dragon who flies high above the Netherwing Fields, where his young dare not land for fear of the Dragonmaw. He is a father in grief. The orcs have taken many of his children to Dragonmaw Fortress and tortured them until they gave in, and his mate Karynaku is chained atop its walls; every attempt he has made to free her has failed. Neltharaku feels powerless against them. It was Illidan, he says, who found the Dragonmaw their leader, Zuluhed, the orc held responsible for the capture of the Dragon Aspect Alexstrasza. If such an orc could take an Aspect, how could the young Netherwing resist him?
sources: quest 10811 description (patron soars high above)

notes: Fact-check: the refusal to land belongs to his young (npc_text 10614), not to Neltharaku. Zuluhed capturing Alexstrasza kept as his words (wiki credits Nekros under Zuluhed's command). Faction template 7 is neutral to both.

title: Overlord Mor'ghor
body: Overlord Mor'ghor rules the Dragonmaw Base Camp on Netherwing Ledge, a coarse and boastful fel orc who serves Illidan and drives his workers to strip the island bare. He was once a chief lieutenant of the Dragonmaw at Grim Batol on Azeroth, a past the black dragonflight has not forgotten. Recruits who arrive with service papers start as peons, and the few who survive rise in rank under his eye. He sends his captains against the Legion on the Twilight Ridge and his commanders against the Aldor and the Scryers. He also keeps dealings of his own: the Netherwing eggs his orcs collect are sought by Lady Sinestra, who speaks for a black dragon master Mor'ghor had believed dead.
sources: quest 11013 description and reward text (service papers, peon)
creature_text 23284 (Lady Sinestra: chief lieutenant at Grim Batol; the Netherwing eggs; my master) and 23139 (The master? He lives?)

title: Illidari Lord Balthas
body: Illidari Lord Balthas is an eredar in Illidan's service who stands among the Dragonmaw at their base camp on Netherwing Ledge. His brother, Reth'hedron the Subduer, chose the other side and now lords over the Twilight Ridge in Nagrand for the Burning Legion. With the Sha'tar bringing war to the gates of the Black Temple, Balthas admits that the Illidari cannot spare the strength to slay an eredar of his brother's power. He has a colder answer instead: a soul cannon attuned to his own blood, which is also Reth'hedron's, to drive his brother back through the Twilight Portal. Reth'hedron will return, Balthas warns, but the Legion's war is weakened for now.
sources: quest 11089 description (Reth'hedron lords over the Twilight Ridge; no resources to slay him with the war the Sha'tar brought to the Black Temple; banish him through the portal)

title: Doomwalker
body: Doomwalker is a fel reaver unlike any other, a towering war engine of the Burning Legion that Kil'jaeden sent to assault the gates of the Black Temple. The tales say it was infused with the captured souls of martyred draenei, which set it apart from the lesser reavers of Outland. It prowls the approaches before the temple and greets intruders in a cold, mechanical voice, warning them to proceed no farther or be eliminated. When it strikes, it speaks of tectonic disruption and the ground trembles, and over each fallen foe it pronounces the same verdict: threat level zero, directive accomplished.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Doomwalker (fel reaver sent by Kil'jaeden to assault the gates of the Black Temple, built with captured draenei souls)

title: The Legion's Bombardment
body: Infernals fall on Wildhammer Stronghold and Shadowmoon Village day and night, flung from Legion Hold, and the defenders of both outposts are close to breaking. Wing Commander Nuainn and Blood Guard Gulmok each send a volunteer into the hold in disguise to listen at the Legion's communication device. The news is grim: Warbringer Razuun, speaking for Doom Lord Kazzak, orders the attacks increased and promises infernals enough from the Deathforge. A bomb built from a dead fel reaver's power core destroys the stockpile in the hold. Scouts at Deathforge Tower and Slag Watch then guide the assault on the forge itself, where the summoning ritual is broken and Razuun is slain. His orders point to the true staging ground, Invasion Point: Cataclysm, reached by a teleporter. There Plexi, for the Alliance, and Nakansi, for the Horde, rig a captured fel reaver to smash the Legion's own infernals, and word of the broken siege goes back to Kurdran and Or'barokh.
sources: creature_text 21502, 21633 (Razuun and Jovaan at the communication device)
notes: Verified. Faction 0: 10562 Alliance only (1101), 10595 Horde only (690), one per side. Lead-ins 11044 and 11048 (filed under Nagrand, unused there) not used.

title: The Cipher of Damnation
body: At the Altar of Damnation the Earthen Ring sets out to heal Shadowmoon's tortured elements. With a totem of spirits, Earthmender Torlok gathers the souls of enraged fire, earth, water and air, and when the spirits finally speak they name Cyrukh the Firelord, an elemental lord unearthed by Gul'dan's ritual. Only the ritual's own words can call him forth. Torlok sends for the hermit Oronok Torn-heart, who confesses that he was Gul'dan's lieutenant: Illidan found those words, the Cipher of Damnation, in the Black Temple and split them among his servants. Oronok's sons go after the pieces. Grom'tor beats one hiding place out of a Coilskar naga. Ar'tor is found dead at Illidari Point, yet his spirit wins back his family bow and the second piece from Veneratus the Many. Borak baits Illidan's envoy with bloodthistle, delivers false orders into Eclipse Point, and ambushes Ruul the Darkener for the third. Read whole at the altar, the cipher calls Cyrukh, and the firelord falls.
sources: quests 10680/10681 (breadcrumbs to Torlok), 10458, 10480, 10481 and creature_text 21024 (spirits name Cyrukh, an elemental lord unearthed)
quests 10513-10519, npc_text 10313-10318 (Oronok's story)
quests 10521-10523 (Grom'tor), 10527-10541 (Ar'tor, Lohn'goron, Veneratus), 10546-10579 (Borak, bloodthistle, Icarius, Ruusk, Ruul)
quest 10588 (reading the cipher at the Altar of Damnation, Cyrukh)
notes: Verified. 10680 Alliance and 10681 Horde breadcrumbs plus 10458 (Torlok, both) as entry points. Torlok's closing hint (another knows the cipher) left out. Wilda's escort 10451 is mentioned under Coilskar Point only.

title: The Return of Teron Gorefiend
body: The ghosts of Shadowmoon have grown restless. Zorus the Judicator at Wildhammer Stronghold and Chief Apothecary Hildagard at Shadowmoon Village craft goggles from ever-burning ash that let their wearers see the dead, and the spirits cleared from both outposts whisper one name: Teron Gorefiend, Gul'dan's warlock, whose soul was bound into a slain knight's body to make the first death knight of the Horde. The trail leads to an ancient Shadowmoon spirit at the Altar of Shadows, who claims Gorefiend took his own life after the Second War and offers to divine his fate if his relics are found. His armor lies with Vhel'kur over Netherwing Ledge, his cloak with the ghosts of the clerics he murdered at Karabor, his truncheon with the Ghostriders who rose from his slain death knights. Once all three are gathered, the spirit drops its mask. It is Gorefiend himself, imprisoned at the altar, and he seizes his helper's body to slay his jailer, Karsius, and walks free once more.
sources: quests 10642, 10643, 10644, 10645 (Alliance, Zorus) and 10624, 10625, 10633, 10639 (Horde, Hildagard)
quest 10625 reward text (Gorefiend slain by Doomhammer, soul placed in a slain knight of Stormwind, first death knight)
quests 10633, 10634, 10635, 10636 (the spirit's account, Vhel'kur, clerics of Karabor, Ghostriders)
quest 10639 description; creature_text 21797, 21872, 21877 (possession, Karsius, Gorefiend has returned)
notes: Verified. Faction 0: 10642 Alliance only, 10624 Horde only. The spirit's claim of suicide is presented as the spirit's tale (the wiki says Turalyon slew him).

title: The Medallion of Karabor
body: The Aldor at the Altar of Sha'tar and the Scryers at the Sanctum of the Stars both learn that the Ashtongue are digging in the Ruins of Baa'ri, and both send agents to seize the Tablets of Baa'ri first. The tablets speak of a Medallion of Karabor, which once let the highest draenei priests enter the temple freely. Orders taken from Oronu the Elder reveal that four fragments of it went to the Ashtongue Corruptors, and once those are won, the trail leads to Akama himself in the Warden's Cage. There his second, Sanoru, admits that Akama has been watching. After the satyr spy Zandras is slain, the visitor is led through a hidden passage to Akama, who confesses that he serves Illidan only in appearance and that the fragments were replicas: he holds the true medallion, still missing its last piece. That search leads into the Arcatraz, onto the Ata'mal Terrace for the Heart of Fury, and at last to A'dal in Shattrath.
sources: quests 10622, 10628 (Sanoru, Zandras, Akama)
quests 10705, 10706, 10707, 10708 (replicas, Udalo in the Arcatraz, Heart of Fury, A'dal)
creature_text 21700 (Heart of Fury, take it to A'dal)
notes: Verified. Aldor/Scryer split: entry points 10568 (Aldor, Ceyla) and 10683 (Scryers, Thelis), plus 10622 (Sanoru, neutral, after both converge). The Black Temple attunement (10944-10985, via A'dal and Xi'ri) is left to Shattrath and only hinted.

title: Illidan's Pupil
body: Aldor and Scryer scouts alike report Sunfury recruits streaming into the Ruins of Karabor, dressed and fighting like Illidan himself. Glaives taken from the initiates confirm the fear: Illidan is training blood elf demon hunters. While the pit lord Azaloth, loosed on his captors, keeps the grounds in chaos, Exarch Onaala and Larissa Sunstrike send their agent to Nagrand to seek Altruis the Sufferer, a demon hunter who bears Illidan no allegiance. Altruis tells the tale of Varedis. Of five warriors Kael'thas sent to Illidan, three died in training and one went mad; Varedis alone survived and soon surpassed the three masters set to teach him. He had stolen into the Shadow Council and learned by heart the Book of Fel Names, said to hold the true name of every demon. After proving themselves to Altruis, the agents take the book from the Shadow Labyrinth, and when Varedis takes his demon form at Karabor it is burned before him, stripping his power as he and his masters fall.
sources: npc_text 10492-10497 (Altruis's account of Varedis)
quests 10641, 10646, 10649, 10668, 10669 (Altruis's trials and the Book of Fel Names)
notes: Fact-check: Altruis 'owes Illidan nothing' contradicted his respect for Illidan (10668), now 'bears no allegiance' (10640). Aldor and Scryer split confirmed: 10587 needs Aldor Friendly (932), 10687 Scryers Friendly (934). Nagrand quests 10640, 10689, 10646 not used as triggers; Nagrand's Altruis person (351828) is not retold.

title: The Plight of the Netherwing
body: Mordenai finds the nether drakes over the Netherwing Fields starving, too frightened to land, and asks for help feeding them flayer carcasses. That kindness reaches their patron, Neltharaku, who tells of Dragonmaw Fortress, where the Dragonmaw torture captured drakes into obedience, and of his mate Karynaku, chained atop its walls. To buy him time, the orcs in the fortress are cut down while he devises a remedy. From nethervine crystals gathered on Netherwing Ledge he makes charms filled with his own essence, which break the riders' hold over their enslaved drakes and set them free to turn on their captors. Then comes the climb to the top of the fortress. Karynaku, weakened by her chains, calls Zuluhed the Whacked to her with a false promise to obey, and when the old chieftain appears he is slain for his key. Freed at last, she carries her rescuer back to Mordenai, who names the stranger kin to the Netherwing Dragonflight.
sources: npc_text 10614-10616 (Neltharaku's tale)
creature_text 11980 (Zuluhed)
notes: Verified. Single neutral entry point. 10872 (an unused copy of Zuluhed the Whacked) ignored.

title: Among the Dragonmaw
body: Sworn by blood oath to the Netherwing, an ally is cloaked by the flight's magic as a fel orc and sent to Netherwing Ledge with service papers for Overlord Mor'ghor, who laughs and makes the newcomer a peon. Daily labor for Taskmaster Varkule covers the true work, done for Yarzill the Merc, a Netherwing agent in disguise: poisoning peon camps, ambushing transporters on the Dragonmaw Skyway, and hunting stolen Netherwing eggs. The infiltrator rises to overseer, captain and commander. Ordered to sack the Aldor or Scryer outpost, the commander warns them instead, and their defenders spring a trap on the Dragonmaw raiders while Mor'ghor is shown medals as proof of victory. At last Mor'ghor names his finest orc the first highlord of the Dragonmaw, and Illidan himself comes to the ledge to see this hero. He sees through the disguise at once and declares the whole operation compromised. Yarzill snatches the highlord to safety, and the Netherwing's thanks wait with Barthamus in Shattrath.
sources: creature_text 23139, 22083, 23141 (Mor'ghor, Illidan, Yarzill at the highlord ceremony)
quest 11019 reward text (Yarzill's eyes flicker blue: we are here with you)
notes: Verified. 11012 Blood Oath is QuestType 0 (auto-complete), so it gets QUEST_DONE; 11013 is the first accepted quest. Neutral entry; the Aldor/Scryer turn (11094/11099) is told as shared history. Barthamus (Shattrath) is only mentioned.

title: The Dark Conclave
body: Journal pages taken from the arakkoa ghosts of the Sketh'lon Wreckage, by Gryphonrider Kieran's agents for the Alliance or Sergeant Kargrul's for the Horde, speak of a spell gone awry and of a deserter. The deserter is Parshah, a haunted arakkoa waiting by the road through the Magma Fields. He tells how his people, seeing the Horde mass under Gul'dan, prepared to strike him first, and how the warlock answered with magic that destroyed their camps and twisted their spirits. Worse, Gul'dan's power fed on the arakkoa's own spell, and the ghosts of the Dark Conclave now seek to summon an ancient evil in the lava pits south of their base camp. Parshah builds a staff to stop them from Asghar's war totem, the Rod of Lianthe taken from Eclipse Point and Sketh'lon feathers, its headpiece charged with the echoes of Gul'dan at the Altar of Damnation. With it the ritual is broken, and Parshah at last believes he was right to desert.
sources: quests 10569, 10759 (Alliance) and 10760, 10761 (Horde)
quests 10777, 10778, 10780, 10782, 10808 (Parshah's staff and the ritual)
npc_text 10556 (Parshah's gaze)
notes: Verified. Faction 0: 10569 Alliance only, 10760 Horde only.

title: The Illidari-Bane Blade
body: Shards of a strange metal turn up among the mo'arg of Legion Hold, etched with glowing runes. Ordinn Thunderfist at Wildhammer Stronghold and Grokom Deatheye at Shadowmoon Village know the work: a rare ore enchanted to destroy demons, a secret weapon the Legion means to use against Illidan's forces. More of the metal is taken from the glaives of the pit lords Makazradon and Morgroron, but forging it is beyond either smith. Both send the ingots to David Wayne, a blacksmith who came to Draenor with the Sons of Lothar and later left the expedition to live alone in Terokkar Forest; even Grokom admits it pains him to send Horde business to a human. Wayne needs rare things: an overcharged manacell from the Mechanar, the Lexicon Demonica from the Shadow Labyrinth, underworld loam from the Steamvault and the Tear of the Earthmother from the Shattered Halls. The finished sword is quenched in the Scalding Pools of the Hand of Gul'dan, a blade to cut down Illidari and Legion demons alike.
sources: quests 10664, 10665, 10666, 10667, 10670, 10676, 10679 (David Wayne's materials, quenching at the Scalding Pools)
npc_text 10500 (David Wayne and the Sons of Lothar)
notes: Verified. Faction 0: 10621 Alliance only, 10623 Horde only (both start from an item). All the chain's quests are filed under Shadowmoon, so it is told here; Terokkar may write David Wayne (21465, Wayne's Refuge) as a TALK person but should not reuse these quests.
